title.narrative: Denmark's Contribution to the 20th Replenishment of the International Development Association (IDA20)

description.narrative:
Based on the IDA20 Final Replenishment Report, “Building Back Better from the Crisis –Toward a Green, Resilient and Inclusive Future”, alongside the Danish organisational strategy for the World Bank, the following results can be noted in relation the Danish priorities:
IDA20 will support countries to emerge in line with the Green, Resilient and Inclusive Development (GRID) framework, by working with three key dimensions:
Green: Increasing climate finance and supporting countries to source nature-based solutions, transition key systems for low-carbon development, create green jobs, and green entire sectors, including finance.
Resilient: Supporting countries to strengthen crisis preparedness, bolster food security, tackle the drivers of Fragility, Conflict and Violence (FCV), address debt vulnerabilities, mobilize domestic revenue, build quality infrastructure, and seize long-term economic opportunities to sustain growth in a post-COVID-19 world.
Inclusive: Supporting countries to address the needs of the poorest and most vulnerable, reduce structural inequalities, and mitigate rising FCV risks through policies and investments that build human capital, strengthen service delivery, close gender gaps, create jobs (including green and decent jobs), and narrow the growing digital divide.
Within the green, resilient and inclusive framework, the following special themes are highlighted as issues:
1) Human capital: Health, education, and safety nets, including disability inclusion.
2) Climate change: Climate Co-Benefits, mitigation, adaptation, sustainable energy, green financing, ecosystems and biodiversity.
3) Gender and development: Economic inclusion, childcare, gender gaps in digital technology, women's land rights, and high skilled employment opportunities for women.
4) Fragility, conflict and violence (FCV): Core governance institutions, refugees, transboundary drivers and crisis recovery.
5) Jobs and Economic Transformation (JET): Resil

IDA is deepening its support to drive a resilient recovery for the poorest countries through its historic $93 billion 20th replenishment cycle (IDA20) between July 1, 2022 and June 30, 2025. With a focus on Building Back Better from the Crisis: Towards a Green, Resilient and Inclusive Future, IDA20 will help countries respond to the multiple challenges in a post-COVID-19 world and restore their trajectory towards achieving the 2030 development goals, ultimately reducing extreme poverty and improving shared prosperity. This overarching theme will be supported by five special themes and four cross cutting issues. The special themes are Human Capital; Climate Change; Gender and Development; Fragility, Conflict, and Violence; and Jobs and Economic Transformation. The four cross-cutting issues are Crisis Preparedness; Governance and Institutions; Debt; and Technology.
